brief_summary: Split cross-section diagram. Left panel, Hall-effect: a magnet above a flat sensor plate, field lines passing straight through it into a voltage-out readout. Right panel, TMR: the same magnet above a three-layer magnetic tunnel junction stack (free layer with a rotating arrow, thin insulating barrier, pinned layer with a fixed arrow) into a resistance-out readout. Visualizes the article's central distinction: a voltage the field generates versus a resistance the field changes.
data_sources: tmr-switches-deep-dive.mdx § 'The same magnet, a different question asked of it' — 'A Hall-effect sensor ... develops a small voltage across itself when a magnetic field passes through it ... TMR asks a structurally different question ... it reads the electrical resistance of a device whose resistance the field changes.'

tmr-switches-deep-dive.mdx § 'Inside the junction' — 'two ultra-thin ferromagnetic layers separated by an insulating barrier a few nanometers thick ... One layer is pinned in a fixed orientation as a reference. The other is free to rotate with whatever external field reaches it.'
https://wiki.dfrobot.com/tutorial/21072 — magnetic tunnel junction structure (free layer, insulating barrier, pinned layer) and spin-dependent tunneling mechanism, cited inline via <Source>
